name: Municipality of Anchorage ADRC
description: Alaska’s Aging and Disability Resource Centers connect seniors, people with disabilities and caregivers with long-term services and supports, regardless of age or income, through regional offices. Specialists pre-screen in person, at home, by phone or by video.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. The statewide ADRC number, 1-855-565-2017, also reaches a specialist. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.

name: Alaska Office of the Long Term Care Ombudsman
organization: Alaska Office of the Long Term Care Ombudsman
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this borough or census area: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and borough or census area. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

source_evidence.title: Alaska Long Term Care Ombudsman brochure (Alaska Legislature document library)
source_evidence.scope: 3745 Community Park Loop, Suite 200, Anchorage; (907) 334-4480 or (800) 730-6393 toll free; akoltco@alaska.gov; search excerpt. The Alaska Commission on Aging lists the same toll-free line (https://aging.alaska.gov; search excerpt). The program is statewide, so every borough and census area shows it.
